passages.text: Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah with crimson-stained garments? Who is this robed in splendor, marching in the greatness of His strength? “It is I, proclaiming vindication, mighty to save.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker sees someone coming from Edom.
This person comes from Bozrah.
His garments are stained red.
He wears splendid clothing.
He marches with great strength.
He answers, “I speak in righteousness.
I am mighty to save.”
passages.original: מִי־ זֶ֣ה׀ בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם חֲמ֤וּץ בְּגָדִים֙ מִבָּצְרָ֔ה זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ צֹעֶ֖ה בְּרֹ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: Why are Your clothes red, and Your garments like one who treads the winepress?
passages.sermon:
The speaker sees a figure.
The figure’s clothes are red.
The speaker asks the figure a question.
The speaker says, “Why are Your clothes red?”
The speaker also asks, “Why do Your garments look like someone who treads the winepress?”
passages.original: מַדּ֥וּעַ אָדֹ֖ם לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּבְגָדֶ֖יךָ כְּדֹרֵ֥ךְ בְּגַֽת׃

passages.text: “I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with Me. I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury; their blood spattered My garments, and all My clothes were stained.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the Lord.
The Lord says, “I have trodden the winepress alone.
No one from the nations was with Me.
I trampled the nations in My anger.
I trod them down in My fury.
Their blood spattered My garments.
All My clothes became stained.”
passages.original: פּוּרָ֣ה׀ דָּרַ֣כְתִּי לְבַדִּ֗י וּמֵֽעַמִּים֙ אֵֽין־ אִ֣ישׁ אִתִּ֔י וְאֶדְרְכֵ֣ם בְּאַפִּ֔י וְאֶרְמְסֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְיֵ֤ז נִצְחָם֙ עַל־ בְּגָדַ֔י וְכָל־ מַלְבּוּשַׁ֖י אֶגְאָֽלְתִּי׃

passages.text: For the day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year of My redemption had come.
passages.sermon: God speaks in this passage.\r\nGod says He held a day of vengeance in His heart.\r\nGod says the year of His redemption arrived.
passages.original: כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם בְּלִבִּ֑י וּשְׁנַ֥ת גְּאוּלַ֖י בָּֽאָה׃

passages.text: I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that no one assisted. So My arm brought Me salvation, and My own wrath upheld Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD looked for help.
He saw no one to help Him.
He was appalled because no one supported Him.
His own arm brought Him salvation.
His own wrath gave Him strength.
passages.original: וְאַבִּיט֙ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵ֔ר וְאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֖ם וְאֵ֣ין סוֹמֵ֑ךְ וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע לִי֙ זְרֹעִ֔י וַחֲמָתִ֖י הִ֥יא סְמָכָֽתְנִי׃

passages.text: I trampled the nations in My anger; in My wrath I made them drunk and poured out their blood on the ground.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God acts with anger and wrath.
God tramples the nations in His anger.
God makes the nations drunk in His wrath.
God pours out their blood on the ground.
passages.original: וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י וַאֲשַׁכְּרֵ֖ם בַּחֲמָתִ֑י וְאוֹרִ֥יד לָאָ֖רֶץ נִצְחָֽם׃ס

passages.text: I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts, because of all that the LORD has done for us— the many good things for the house of Israel according to His great compassion and loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is loving and devoted.
The LORD does praiseworthy acts.
I will tell about the LORD’s loving devotion.
I will tell about the LORD’s praiseworthy acts.
The LORD has done many things for us.
The LORD has done many good things for the house of Israel.
The LORD acts with great compassion.
The LORD acts with much loving devotion.
passages.original: חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה׀ אַזְכִּיר֙ תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כְּעַ֕ל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה וְרַב־ טוּב֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ גְּמָלָ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמָ֖יו וּכְרֹ֥ב חֲסָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: For He said, “They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal.” So He became their Savior.
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the people of Israel.
He said, “These are My people.”
He called them His sons.
He said, “They will not be disloyal.”
God became their Savior.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַךְ־ עַמִּ֣י הֵ֔מָּה בָּנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יְשַׁקֵּ֑רוּ וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְמוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and compassion He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
passages.sermon:
God cared for the people of Israel.
When they suffered, God also felt their pain.
The Angel of God's Presence saved them.
God loved them.
God showed them compassion.
God redeemed them.
God lifted them up.
God carried them through all the days of old.
passages.original: בְּֽכָל־ צָרָתָ֣ם׀ לֹא צָ֗ר וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ פָּנָיו֙ הֽוֹשִׁיעָ֔ם בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ וּבְחֶמְלָת֖וֹ ה֣וּא גְאָלָ֑ם וַֽיְנַטְּלֵ֥ם וַֽיְנַשְּׂאֵ֖ם כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: But they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit. So He turned and became their enemy, and He Himself fought against them.
passages.sermon:
God chose Israel as His people.
God gave them His Holy Spirit.
The people rebelled against God.
They grieved His Holy Spirit.
God turned against them.
God became their enemy.
God Himself fought against them.
passages.original: וְהֵ֛מָּה מָר֥וּ וְעִצְּב֖וּ אֶת־ ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ וַיֵּהָפֵ֥ךְ לָהֶ֛ם לְאוֹיֵ֖ב ה֥וּא נִלְחַם־ בָּֽם׃

passages.text: Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses. Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is the One who set His Holy Spirit among them, who sent His glorious arm to lead them by the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to gain for Himself everlasting renown, who led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?
passages.sermon:
God led the people of Israel in ancient times.
He acted during the days of Moses.
The people remembered those days.
God brought His people through the sea.
He led them with the shepherds of His flock.
God placed His Holy Spirit among them.
He sent His glorious arm to guide them.
He led them by the right hand of Moses.
God divided the waters before His people.
He did this to make His name known forever.
God led them through the deep places.
He guided them like a horse in the wilderness.
They did not stumble as they went.
passages.original: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר יְמֵֽי־ עוֹלָ֖ם מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ אַיֵּ֣ה׀ הַֽמַּעֲלֵ֣ם מִיָּ֗ם אֵ֚ת רֹעֵ֣י צֹאנ֔וֹ אַיֵּ֛ה הַשָּׂ֥ם בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ אֶת־ ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ מוֹלִיךְ֙ לִימִ֣ין מֹשֶׁ֔ה זְר֖וֹעַ תִּפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ בּ֤וֹקֵֽעַ מַ֙יִם֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ שֵׁ֥ם עוֹלָֽם׃ מוֹלִיכָ֖ם בַּתְּהֹמ֑וֹת כַּסּ֥וּס בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ׃

passages.text: Like cattle going down to the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. You led Your people this way to make for Yourself a glorious name.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit of the LORD gave rest to His people.
The people were like cattle going down to the valley.
The LORD led His people in this way.
He did this to make for Himself a glorious name.
passages.original: כַּבְּהֵמָה֙ בַּבִּקְעָ֣ה תֵרֵ֔ד ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה תְּנִיחֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֚ן נִהַ֣גְתָּ עַמְּךָ֔ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְךָ֖ שֵׁ֥ם תִּפְאָֽרֶת׃

passages.text: Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation. Where are Your zeal and might? Your yearning and compassion for me are restrained.
passages.sermon:
God, You live in heaven.
Your home is holy and glorious.
Look down from heaven.
See us from Your holy and glorious place.
Where is Your zeal?
Where is Your power?
Your deep feelings and compassion for me are held back.
passages.original: הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִזְּבֻ֥ל קָדְשְׁךָ֖ וְתִפְאַרְתֶּ֑ךָ אַיֵּ֤ה קִנְאָֽתְךָ֙ וּגְב֣וּרֹתֶ֔ךָ הֲמ֥וֹן מֵעֶ֛יךָ וְֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ אֵלַ֥י הִתְאַפָּֽקוּ׃

passages.text: Yet You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, O LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from Everlasting is Your name.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our Father.
Abraham does not know us.
Israel does not acknowledge us.
The LORD is our Father.
The LORD is our Redeemer.
The LORD’s name is Redeemer from Everlasting.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֤י אַבְרָהָם֙ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֔נוּ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֣א יַכִּירָ֑נוּ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אָבִ֔ינוּ גֹּאֲלֵ֥נוּ מֵֽעוֹלָ֖ם שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Why, O LORD, do You make us stray from Your ways and harden our hearts from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage.
passages.sermon:
The people speak to the LORD.
They call Him by name.
They ask the LORD a question.
They say, "Why do You make us stray from Your ways?"
They say, "Why do You harden our hearts so we do not fear You?"
They ask the LORD to return.
They say, "Return for the sake of Your servants."
They say, "Return for the sake of the tribes that belong to You."
passages.original: לָ֣מָּה תַתְעֵ֤נוּ יְהוָה֙ מִדְּרָכֶ֔יךָ תַּקְשִׁ֥יחַ לִבֵּ֖נוּ מִיִּרְאָתֶ֑ךָ שׁ֚וּב לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ שִׁבְטֵ֖י נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For a short while Your people possessed Your holy place, but our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary.
passages.sermon: God’s people are holy.\r\nYour people possessed Your holy place for a short time.\r\nOur enemies trampled Your sanctuary.
passages.original: לַמִּצְעָ֕ר יָרְשׁ֖וּ עַם־ קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ צָרֵ֕ינוּ בּוֹסְס֖וּ מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: We have become like those You never ruled, like those not called by Your name.
passages.sermon:
We are the people of God.
God once ruled over us.
Now we have become like people God never ruled.
We are like those who do not bear God’s name.
God’s name is not called upon us.
passages.original: הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא־ מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא־ נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם
